traits: Cap 3 to 12 cm, felted, bright red and paler at the edge, finely cracked when mature
Pores yellow then olive-yellow, usually bluish when bruised
Stem 3 to 10 cm, yellow or red, often bulbous; small red or orange dots at the very base
Whitish to pale yellow flesh, sometimes slightly bluish under the cap; mild taste
Under broadleaf trees, in parks, gardens, clearings and roadsides, on chalky soil
safetyNote: Not recommended: the DGfM lists it and Wikipedia (fr) calls it edible after cooking, young firm ones with the stem removed, but to be avoided in urban areas where it absorbs pollutants; Wikipedia (en) says edible but often maggoty, poor, listed as not recommended and its edibility questioned. The most prudent status is kept. Wikipedia (fr) separates it from several small boletes of no food interest, Xerocomellus ripariellus and X. redeuilhii among them.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
